author: Mativh
subject: Potential Priest Changes: New Abilities, Talents, Passives
content_md:
**Shadow:**

Dispersion
'Improved Fade' talent renamed & reworked, 2 ranks
![Image](https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/spell_magic_lesserinvisibilty.jpg)
For the duration of Fade, your Mana will regenerate at a 15/30% rate while casting, the rate is doubled while in Shadowform.

Instead of the new Improved Shadowform (a level 60 passive granting -15% mana cost and +15% mana regen while casting), I propose a more dynamic solution to the Priest mana-gement issue.
Ethereal Fade would be accessible while levelling, which is the part of gameplay many Turtles focus on.
An active, spellcaster way of gaining mana (and an alternative to the 5sec-rule-wanding) would be most welcome.

Soothing Shadows
Shadow talent, next to 'Vampiric Touch', with it as a prerequisite. 2 ranks.
![Image](https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/spell_nzinsanity_chasedbyshadows.jpg)
Casting Shadowmend on a friendly target applies on them the Soothing Shadows buff, which increases the healing received from subsequent Shadowmends by 2/4% and from Vampiric Embrace by 10/20%.
Lasts 2 minutes, stacks up to 5 times.

Similarly to Shadow Weaving, the stacking and effect is shared, not bound to the caster (also allowing multiple Priests to cooperate at effective hybrid dps/healing).
Shadow healing; Holy can mend and harm, so can Shadow, although both approach it in different ways.
With Shadowmend and Vampiric Embrace, it is possible to have an alternative shadow-healer/damage-dealer/utility playstyle.
Specializing at the expense of things is one way to go, but the jack-of-all-trades-master-of-none vanilla class design and less rigid roles could also be explored.

When it comes to Shadow aoe, I think that could be depending on the races lore.
But if there was a generic one, reverse Holy Nova makes the most sense, one that does not radiate holy energy outwards, but instead absorbs shadows from the surrounding, in the process damaging nearby units and restoring some mana (depending on the number of affected targets) instead of healing like Holy Nova;

 **Holy:**

Holy Word: Anathema
Holy talent ability
![Image](https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/spell_fire_elementaldevastation.jpg)
Applies 'Anathema' on an enemy for 10 seconds; allowing one Holy healing ability to be cast on the target, but instead of healing, it'll deal half of it's healing value as Holy damage. Against Undeads and Demons, the value is not halved. 45 sec cooldown.

 *Next to Holy Champion, with Spiritual Guidance as a prerequisite (Spiritual Healing position moved sideways out of the way). For all except trolls, the Holy spec in general doesn't fit them.*

Clerics Aid
Holy ability, learned if the Priest learns First Aid
![Image](https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/spell_holy_sealofsacrifice.jpg)
Makes your next bandage twice as effective.

 *Professions and classes interacting is good for immersion, first aid thematically fits holy priests the most, here the healing value of bandages is increased, at exchange for mana. This one could perhaps be a Human Priest racial though.*

Fundamental Forces
Level 1 passive.
![Image](https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/inv_misc_supersoulash.jpg)
Whenever you cast a Holy spell, you receive the debuff Light Rapport, that reduces the effectiveness of all of your Shadow abilities by 10% and gives them a 3% chance to trigger an Arcane Nova.

Whenever you cast a Shadow spell, you receive the debuff Enveloping Shadow, that reduces the effectiveness of all of your Holy abilities by 10% and gives them a 3% chance to trigger one tick of Hellfire.

Both debuffs last 15 seconds and stack up to 5 times.

(effectiveness = healing & damage done)
It is ment to depict the lore behind the forces of Light and Shadow, for the same reason Shadowform locks all holy abilities, it never made sense that a priest would use simultaneously both Light and Shadow without any repercussion, the Arcane Nova is a release of arcane energies and Hellfire a release of Fel energies, from the combination of the seemingly opposing forces of light and shadow, as per the lore where their collision created the Arcane from which the physical world is woven together, and the Fel from which twisting nether came into being. It could be utilized to create a symphony of forces purposefully errupt

It is stated that before life began, before even the cosmos took shape, there was Light ... and there was Shadow. However, the Light, unfettered by the confines of time and space, swelled across all existence in the form of a boundless prismatic sea. Great torrents of living energy flitted through its mirrored depths, their movements conjuring a symphony of joy and hope. The Light's ocean was dynamic and ever shifting. Yet as it grew, some of its energies faded and dimmed, leaving behind pockets of seemingly cold nothingness.

From the absence of Light in these spaces, a new power coalesced and came to be. A dark and vampiric force driven to devour all energy, to twist creation inward to feed upon itself, this power was the Shadow. The Shadow quickly grew and spread its influence, moving against the Light's flowing waves. The mounting tension between these two seemingly opposing yet inseparable energies eventually ignited a series of catastrophic explosions, rupturing the fabric of creation and birthing a new realm into existence. In that moment, the physical universe was born.

The most unstable energies coalesced into an astral dimension known as the Twisting Nether. Light and Shadow collided and bled together at this realm's edges, throwing it into turmoil. Linked to the Great Dark Beyond, although tangentially, the Twisting Nether existed outside the physical universe's borders.

 **Discipline:**

Art Of War
Discipline talent, 5 ranks
![Image](https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/inv_staff_08.jpg)
Increases your staff skill by 1/2/3/4/5 and your unarmed skill by 2/4/6/8/10. Additionally, your melee critical hits cause you to enter into 'Flow State' for 15 seconds, during which your dodge chance and hit chance are increased by 5%, stacks up to 3 times.

Patience
Discipline talent, next to Unbreakable Will, with it as a prerequisite, 1 rank
![Image](https://wow.zamimg.com/images/wow/icons/large/spell_arcane_focusedpower.jpg)
After a movement impairing effect, or a silence applied on you ends, your attack power is increased by up to 25% of your total Spirit for 10 seconds.

 *The discipline talent tree was originally ment to be a melee spec, resembling the archetype of a Monk (not the MoP one), it was nice to see the inner fire change - granting attack power like it did in W3.*

They're generic for all Priests, ment to enhance the class and be integrated into it, other ideas I've reserved for specific races.
They might serve as an inspiration for the potential upcoming priest changes, feel free to suggest improvements & contructive criticism.

content_md:
> **Zirek wrote: Fri Oct 13, 2023 1:59 pm**
> Balance is overrated. Do you really think people play Vanilla Wow because it's the very balanced MMO ? In Vanilla Wow balance was totally mess but they cared adding cool stuff instead and this is why people prefer Vanilla over the other versions of Wow.

Back in Vanilla, there was no shortage of folks who were clamoring about how weak or strong certain classes/specs were (aka balance issues) and this is no different today. So, yes, I think balance is always something to keep an eye on and even moreso given the recent announcement of a dedicated PvP server.

With regards to adding 'cool stuff', well this is obviously a subjective concept. As already mentioned, the OP (and myself) consider those things to be interesting ideas. The real question is, do the TWoW staff and the bulk of the community feel the same way?

What I'd also like to point out is that homogenisation is the path we should avoid at all costs. In my opinion, the later versions of the game (and, yes, I'd even include TBC in this) ventured down this path all too often. So, when you give a few of your 'interesting' ideas;

> **Zirek wrote: Fri Oct 13, 2023 1:59 pm**
> They should add more intersting stuff like shadowform gives stealth to priests at night time or fade gives invisiblity or maybe makes them immune to physical damage. Maybe they can even add void tendrils from Mop.

My immediate reaction is;
 1) why would you give some sort of 'stealth' or 'invisibility' to another class? I'm sure the Rogues and Druids would love that....
 2) Void Tendrils? An AoE root? I'm sure the Mages would love that....
 3) nothing to do with homogenisation, but 'immunity' to physical damage!? Fade lasts 10 seconds. Whilst it might sound fun for the priest, it's very uninteractive/unengaging for classes like Warriors/Rogues who primarily deal physical damage...

It's quite easy to come up with these 'interesting' ideas of yours but they tend to fall foul of homogenisation/balance issues. So, in my opinion, I think the OP's ideas satisfy the following criteria:
 1) Interesting (debatable but, in my opinion, yes)
 2) Don't break immersion/roleplaying elements of the game
 3) Maintaining class identify (i.e. don't lead to, if any, homogenisation)
 3) Don't cause massive balance issues from a design perspective (obviously, the numbers themselves would require tweaking)

author: Mativh
subject: Re: Suggestions for Priest Changes: New Abilities, Talents, Passives
content_md:
> **Zirek wrote: Wed Oct 11, 2023 6:13 pm**
> Boring you really don't understand what makes vanilla wow is vanilla wow..

I've stated that I'm not trying to reinvent the class, but integrate these ideas into the existing structure, while leaving the more impactful/flavorful ones for specific races that I'll post in the future.
And they're ment to be considerable for implementation.

Ethereal Fade - allowing the Priest to utilize it's spells (while levelling) instead of having to resort to wanding (unlike other spellcasters) is as boring/interesting as the Priests spells are themselves.

Soothing Shadows - adds to the Shadow tree an alternative build, which can be coordinated with other Priests to bring forth a healer/dps hybrid playstyle.

Holy Word: Anathema - A possibility to turn the diverse array of healing abilities into offensive ones and use them situationally, making the priest especially capable against undeads and demons.

Clerics Aid - Intertwining professions and classes/races, this one turns First Aid into an unique healing build support.

Fundamental Forces - makes the spells of choice matter more, mixing two schools of magic has both it's cost and benefit and so does staying purely in one of them, the lore behind it is well written and it's a very abstract concept which I believe would be well conveyed through this passive

> **Zirek wrote: Wed Oct 11, 2023 6:13 pm**
> They should add more intersting stuff like shadowform gives stealth to priests at night time or fade gives invisiblity or maybe makes them immune to physical damage. Maybe they can even add void tendrils from Mop.

Shadowform stealth - Lore-wise it'd make no sense to add it mindlessly to all Priests, only some of the Forsaken Shadow Ascendants have reached that level of mastery, and even then it'd not depend on the lack of daylight, as the deepest shadows are cast by the strongest light.
Which brings me to:

Fade invisibility/invulnerability - The Shadow Priest doesn't manipulate the forces from which reality is woven together in order to remove itself from sight (like arcane mages), nor is it partially shifting to another plane (like a demon would), nor literally sneaks like a cat or a rogue. Fade is somewhat a psychic concept, not only literally fading just because.. it is a good candidate for Shadow Priest pseudo-stealth but not randomly, as mentioned above.

Void Tendrils - the only part of the lore before cataclysm where something similar is mentioned is when Forsaken Shadow Ascendants go beyond the regular Shadowform, and even then it isn't an universal Old God tentacle (a simplified copy of the Lovecraftian Old Gods), instead it is a result of a huge cataclysm retcon by Activision that erased all shadow priest lore and turned them into voidlord/old god cultists.
If you enjoy that in retail they expanded on it quite a bit.
But Turtle WoW builds a coherent and immersive world that is true to the franchise as it was envisioned by the original developers, before corporate greed and parent companies ruined it.

author: Quidoba
subject: Re: Shadowpriests in PVE?
content_md:
When it comes to mana issues, shadow priest on TWOW plays a lot more like a mage in classic than a shadow priest in classic.  You don't have infinite mana, but it is pretty manageable, and gets better and better as you accumulate more gear.

The difference is attributable to: <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?spell=45553>

Just like in classic, you don't need to get as much hit. Also crit is of little value. So you can itemize for some mp5 and even spirit (you can get 30% regen while casting due to improved shadow form + talents).

In low end gear, I see shadow priests consistently out-damage mages and warlocks (re-itemization of mage and warlock t1 might level this difference).  At high end gear, shadow priests begin to fall behind.  At high end gear, smite spec actually out damages shadow spec, but you probably lose more utility for the overall raid than is worth the small dps bump.  Smite is fun to do on raids you have on farm.

Priests are pretty well PVE balanced on TWOW imo. Spriests slap in pvp.

author: Zvyrhol
subject: Is Holy Resistance real?
content_md:
I was reading a document today about spell resistances and spell hit calculations, you can read it here if you are interested: <https://royalgiraffe.github.io/resist-guide>

While reading this wall of text, I came across reference:

> *There is also Holy, but almost no effects add Holy Resistance so is almost always 0, with an exception of NPCs having level-based resistance to Holy as discussed later.*

This puzzled me because until now I thought Holy Resistance didn't exist or even if it did exist, it was always equal to 0. So I googled some topics regarding Holy Resistance and it seems that every enemy gets +5 to all resistances multiplied by level difference between enemy and you (this works only if your enemy has higher level than you). So raid bosses, which are lv 63, have always +15 extra resistances against you. The most interesting thing is that these resistances seem to include Holy Resistance - this resistance should affect your holy spells so they will be resisted more often.

I haven't tested this yet so I write this post. Would be cool if fellow Smite priests or people who know resistances well, confirm my discovery.

EDIT:
Conclusion regarding Smite priests is that they can have up to +16% bonus spell hit in order to fully increase the chance to hit the raid bosses, they don't need any item that decreases resistance because level-difference-resistance is impenetrable. They will always have at least 1% miss chance though. It's worth noting that in PVP you can achieve the same thing with only +3% spell hit from items.

FINAL EDIT:
Level-based resistance for holy spells doesn't exist! At least in Turtle WoW. It was removed from the game: [viewtopic.php?p=27521&hilit=holy+resist ... age%20Scar](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=27521&hilit=holy+resistance#p27521:~:text=has%20been%20increased.-,Removed%20level%20based%20resist%20chance%20from%20Holy%20spells.%20Not%20to%20be%20confused%20with%20chance%20to%20miss.,-Ferocious%20Rage%20Scar)
It should still be present in other vanilla private servers/Classic though.

author: Blackduck
subject: Re: Is Holy Resistance real?
content_md:
You can use this macro to check a mobs armor value and resistance levels

/script u=UnitResistance y="target" a=u(y ,0) h=u(y ,1) f=u(y ,2) n=u(y ,3) fr=u(y ,4) s=u(y ,5) z=u(y ,6) SendChatMessage(UnitName(y).." has "..a.." Armor, "..h.." HR, "..f.." FR, "..n.." NR, "..fr.." FrR, "..s.." SR and "..z.." AR.", SAY)

Every enemy in the game including bosses that I've checked has 0 holy resist.

The only enemies in the game that actually "resist" holy spells are chromag and the drakkonoids in bwl but I think that's just a general spell resist and not because they have any holy resistance.  They just never get a weakness to holy magic like they do with other types of spells.

subject: Priest Specific Macro Collection
content_md:
Hello Turtles, I've found several macros that I use on my Priest from various places. Just putting together a collection of these in a post that someone else may find.

 -- Self-Buffs

/script if not buffed("Inner Fire", 'player') then CastSpellByName("Inner Fire") else if not buffed("Power Word: Fortitude", 'player') then CastSpellByName("Power Word: Fortitude",1) end;end

 --Smite

/script if not buffed("Smite", 'target') then CastSpellByName("Smite") end

 --Shoot (Wand)

/script if (UnitName('target')==nil) then TargetNearestEnemy() else if not IsAutoRepeatAction(12) then CastSpellByName("Shoot") end;end

author: Moonstorm
subject: Re: Priest Specific Macro Collection
content_md:
The game in its original form did not allow for a priest to target other groups with Prayer of Healing, such a feature was only added later. Here is how to circumvent this limitation - aside from the one character slot in a group you're swapping into. This solution does not leverage empty slots in groups. Though the ability to switch between groups on the fly can be useful to other classes too, like hunters, shamans and druids, for priests it's proven to be useful when dealing with situations in which there are not an awful lot of healers to go around and a lot of incoming group damage.

Requires Supermacro add-on. Recommended to be used in a culture in which people are not disturbed by raid frames switching around. This can be achieved by using class-based raid frames or unitframe add-ons that allow the the frames to be frozen regardless of changes. Note that there may be unexpected swaps if the size of the raid group changes. The current solution switches you to the bottom-most slot shown to you in a given group.

Make an empty macro called "Back" and place it in action button slot 57. The main macro will write over the "Back" macro each time you switch yourself around. If you use a different one, remember to change the macro itself accordingly. Place the macro below into action button slot 56.

/script tarName = UnitName("target") n = GetNumRaidMembers() for i=n,1,-1 do na, rank, subgroup = GetRaidRosterInfo(i) if na == tarName then do for o=n,1,-1 do local nam, rankk, sg = GetRaidRosterInfo(o) if subgroup == sg then do if nam ~= tarName then do SwapRaidSubgroup(o,n) local macroID = EditMacro(2,nil,nil,"/script PickupAction(56) PlaceAction(57) PlaceAction(56); SwapRaidSubgroup("..o..","..n..");",1); break end end end end end end end end PickupAction(56) PlaceAction(57) PlaceAction(56);

author: Akos1896
subject: Should I level a priest?
content_md:
Hey!

I was thinking about leveling one. Specifically for healing, I am less interested in shadow.
Having a high-raid resto shaman main and I was curious about the other alternatives. TWOW is the first place I met WOW, having very few personal experiences with most of the classes. To compensate for this, watched many tutorials etc, but lacking first hand experience.

I enjoy healing. As a resto shaman I love the added utility of the totems but sometimes I feel that my heals are boring. I can wide heal, quick heal and big heal; and all of the iterations via downgrades. I like keeping things complex, with downgrades I use 10 heals as a shaman but to be real it's three heals on different talent levels. Looked up the priests and I admire the sheer amount of heal and damage prevention they can use. I'm thinking about 'giving up' the utility part my totems are giving for the stamina buff, the shackle, the MC and for the extra heals -> My ideal scenario is when I play a healer with many different heals with downgrades and learning to optimize that huge variety. Several action bars just for heals and the challenge to use them properly is what I want. But this leads to my questions.

 1. How much of the healing and damage prevention is actually being used by priests at raiding? I heard that shields are very situational on tanks because they prevent rage generation. Unsure how good HoTs are or how many heals are actually being used. If priest raiding gameplay is buffing up the team then pressing 1-2 heals then I'd skip leveling one. Currently with shaman I use 3 heals on 10 buttons with downgrades -> my dream would be something which makes healing even more interesting. For example 4-5 healing or damage prevention being frequently used at raids with possible downgrades.

 2. Wide heal. That's something I enjoy a lot with my shammie. Heard that priests have a party heal but with big CD. Do the priests have something which is - while not equivalent to chain heal - can be used to heal many targets at the same time in a raiding environment and can be spammed if necessary? I dont look for an OP ability, it can be mana-inefficient or weak, I just want an additional tool to use under certain scenarios.

 3. Oh no button - shammie's have nature's swiftness which can be used alongside with a healing spell if a heal is needed very fast. Do the priests have a way to very quickly react to an oh no situation?

 4. Raiding niche - I heard that in non-cross faction servers paladins are the spot healers of the alliance and shamans are the raid healers of the horde, while priests take up the other role since both factions can play them. My question is: in a cross-faction environment do the priests have a specific healing role they excel at or they are just behind at palas at tank-healing and behind shamans at wide-healing? I don't have a problem with not leading heal charts but feeling as expendable would stop me from leveling this char. I just have to feel that priests as healers have a specific thing they really excel at in raiding environments to feel a justification to work my dwarfie up to level 60.

 2 - Actually, they have TWO party wide heals. Neither of them have a CD and one even does damage. I'm not sure how viable either are but I think fairly so.

 3 - I don't -think- they have something like that? But like I said, shield can work like a sort of OH SHIT button if you get heals off quickly enough after using it.

 4 - I literally have no idea what the niche is. All I know is priest is great at healing.

Somethin' extra because I'm feeling generous - Don't listen to Majestik. That server's dead and you going there isn't going to satiate his need to advertise it like it's worth anyone's time.

author: Thexdylldolan
subject: Re: Should I level a priest?
content_md:
I raid as a priest in my guild, and I have raided as a holy pally on this server, and priest is a very fun healer, but it's a bit more difficult than other healers IMO, for a couple of reasons
 1. Healing spells are pretty expensive by and large, so until you start popping off with spirit and meditation, mana is a bit intense especially if you're trying to maximize output.
 2. You don't have an "oh shit" button like most other heal classes do, power word shield is close, but its not going to save anyone other than a DPS who draws aggro for a second
The priest kit is very wide, meaning you have to consider all of your spells, and thier applications to get the most from your spells.

Power word shield is a very good spell, it provides over 2k+ effective hp, but yes, rage bar users prefer not to have it. This does not mean it is bad! Its still very good, especially if you have a prot pally, they love that shit.

Priests party heals (prayer of healing and holy nova) have very niche use in raiding, as it is very slow and very expensive, and hopy nova is a meme. Still sees a small amount of use though.

Overall, priest doesn't really have their own special unique role as a healer, but instead they have a wide toolkit to use. Dwarf brings fear ward, which is a big benefit to raids for some content.

From your post it seems you may enjoy priest in raids. Enjoy leveling brother :D

author: Sgadow
subject: Goblins/Gnomes and Priests
content_md:
Hello all!

So I'm bringing this up since Gnomes and Goblins are the ONLY two races in the game that don't have a class they can heal with. While I can understand some of the story behind this, it limits people who enjoy these races and healing from combining the two. My thought on this is simple:

Give them priests.

Why? Because the holy light, in and of itself, is not 'good' and doesn't only answer the call of 'good' people. We have examples of Murlocs using holy smite and the Scarlets as well, neither of which would fall into the realm of 'good' by any stretch of the imagination.

It makes sense that a Gnome could, through their connection with the Dwarves, see the holy light as a beacon of hope or a source of potential power for their mechanations.

Goblins, being greedy, can certainly see the appeal in profit from being a religious leader, healing others, etc. Also, shadow likely falls more in line with goblin greed (and can be easily taught by their forsaken counterparts or trolls).

So I ask the question: Why don't these two races have the class? You don't need new spells for them, give them existing ones.
Gnomes: Desparate Prayer and Fear Ward
Goblins: Shadowguard and Touch of Weakness

author: Imonobor
subject: Priests should be able to wield 2H Maces
content_md:
Yes, I know it sounds a bit out there, but hear me out.
There are a lot of 2H maces that are geared towards paladins that could just as easily be worn by priests - holy damage, int, spirit, all the good stuff, but with a bit of DPS ontop.

Why would priests care about DPS on a melee weapon you say? Melee/wand weaving. Leveling priests utilize this mechanic quite a lot and it provides some really good mana-free DPS to go with your DoTs and shields. But these tactics are basically useless when it comes to the endgame - staves and one-handers just don't have the OOMPH to make it worthwhile, and priests don't really have anything to buff their melee other than Inner Fire.

With the class changes patch coming, I want to build upon this idea and propose that Discipline priests be given more of a Monk or Battle Priest focus - they already have buffs to wands and Inner Fire, so they're best suited for the job. There are a lot of things that could be done to make it work, all the way from paladin-esque melee holy spells to outright pseudo-tank talents.
I'm obviously dreaming big here, but what I want to say is that there is a lot of potential in the Discipline tree, to make it something more than just "that spec with the Power Infusion". I hope the class changes council can utilize some of these ideas.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Shadow Priest Endgame Help
content_md:
Firstly, if you just start out and are in greens, do not go to black morass. That dungeon is difficaultywise somewhere around zg. Get some other gearpieces from easier places before.

With that warning out of the way, the number one item to be aware of is [Nordrannar herbal tea](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=61675) it helps you sustain yourself in pve much better and if you are so inclined is the cheapest consumable for pvping.
Among the easiest way to get it is doing the blooming hyjalroot & stockpiling hyjalroot quests and turning then breaking the shards down with the shard de-harmonisation quest.

Gearwise more is always better, so i wont bore you with any longwinded explanations on what to get. But the best gear available is & most likely always will be from endgame raids.

Shadownmend is quite lackluster as a spell. Its generally not worth using it. If you really need to heal, its better to switch out of shadowform and use proper heals instead. You wont miss it if you dont have it. But its tradeable and sometimes goes for a low price on the AH, but dont waste much gold on it.

If you have the gear, shadowpriest is among the absolutely strongest classes for 1v1. But foe the beginning i can only recommend you try to pick unfair fights :)

subject: ShadowMend/Shadow Mend
content_md:
Let's talk Shadow Mend...

Shadow Mend is a 3 second cast heal, so the scaling should be: 3/3.5s - 85.71%. From testing, the spell coefficient is around 45%.

Can this be corrected to 85.71%?

Or, if the coefficient is going to stay ~45%, then can we get the cast speed to reflect this, 1.5/3.5s - 42.85%?

Additionally, let's take a look at its effectiveness...

The mana cost is 635 mana. Greater Heal has a similar cost in both mana 710 and cast speed 3s but is 4x as effective with no 30s cool down.

Can we get the mana cost reduced or the base heal amount increased?

author: Heroclastus
subject: Re: Disc Priest in PvP > Mitigating resists on fears?
content_md:
Spell hit and resistance are two different things basically. You want 3% spell hit in PvP to make your spells able to hit on same-lvl targets. Increasing spell hit doesn't do anything about resistances however, so putting more than 2 points in shadow focus as priest is pointless in PvP.

The confusion is probably that both a 'miss' from a spell due to low spell hit (e.g. attacking a raid boss with no spell hit gear) and a resist due to enemy resistances show as 'resist' when the spell lands.

To counter the resists on spells which you are probably experiencing against warlocks and priests the most, you need spell penetration (that's the only thing that works there) or a way to lower targets resistances (lock curse e.g.)

author: Svercalirin
subject: Priest Patch - Observations
content_md:
Good afternoon,

After seeing the class changes a few things came up. Lets break it into different aspects:

 **- Shadow Spec:**
Shadow is missing a lot of synergy with other talent trees. Keeping in mind the change on spell coeficients and how you are planning the class to be played. The shadow tree is very uninteresting. As a PVE player you won't go for blackout, imp psychich scream, silence, Imp Mana Burn (unless you have new mechanics, other classes are better for this job). You end up having few options to choose. Meaning, you will end up going into the Disc or Holy Tree and the synergy gets even worse!

Lets start with Discipline: 1st row is very useless for shadow priest. You will get 2 points on wands because the other 2 options doesn't get you any benefit whatsoever. Second tree arguably you may choose different options. 3rd row Improved Inner Fire and Meditation or Inner Focus. If you get to this point, you'd still have 5 points, which you can finish the 2nd row talents you were looking for or go back into shadow spec and get the remaning talents you missed. This will only be for new players or levelers with low spell power, as they would highly benefit from the Imp Inner fire with the rework of inner fire you'd be with +96 spell damage. My recommendation would be to move Unbreakable will to 1st row this allowes better quality of life for shadow priests if they choose to go disc tree as well.

Holy Tree: The goal on this tree is to reach Spiritual Guidance for +30% spell power. This is vialbe if you have more than 384 spirit (this would give you the same amount of spell power that improved Inner Fire gives). Regardless of that, you had to spend 15 points on a tree that you don't get any benefit.

You may have a few variations from this talent tree according to what your necessities: [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/priest?p ... BQAoBAA%3D](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/priest?points=TArCQDAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAFAaoAIANBQAoBAA%3D)

 **- Holy Spec:**
With all base healing values being reduced by 15% for ranks above level 30, priests will need to delve deeper into the tree to get Spiritual Healing.

Lightwell has always been troublesome. Depending on other players to click on a spell to heal is very complicated. On theory is should be fine, but it isn't. Depending on the fight you have, if you are stacked or not... there are many variables and the biggest of all: Will someone stop what they are doing to move near a lightwell and click on it? TBC had a fix for that, which was Prayer of Mending. I am a little skeptical on this ability and also how it will interact. Could it maybe "auto cast" on players bellow 90% hp (prioritizing lower %) and within 30 yrds range?

It would be good to see Proclaim Hero ranks, scaling armor or maybe the all resist as well. It feel very weak the current form. The additional skill are very good.

Divine Fury, would be interesting to have prayer of healing added to it as well... Swift Recovery sells me the concept of priests being tank healers...

Being ableto get all the quality of life from disc makes it very good and interesting.

 - **Discipline:**
Smite Spec? What? We Inquisitors now?

This feels like a very interesting concept. Using shield that breaks to increase spell damage + holy fire for more spell power... It requires a rotation that isn't only spell damage, but interactive with the encounter. This will make the spec not good on some encounters, for example Cthun or Viscidus. I also see a small problem on groups with more than 1 priest with smite spec, as both might not be able to upkeep the bonus from shield.

 **- Racials**
How Dwarves go from the best PVE class due to their racial skill to now being the worse?  Avatar is very useless other than PVP.
Cons:
- It Cost mana.

- I am a caster, what benefit I get from gaining 25% armor (I wear cloth, that is +200 armor)

- I get resist bonus: if I am on an encounter that requires resist, I will get it regarless of having a buff for 15 seconds
Once again, it is a horrible Passive. As a priest you get 0 benefits from it. At least give casting speed or allow it to be casted on friendly players or anything that makes it useful. As a dwarf priest player, this feels like: donate money to get points and reroll a different class.

For PVP I agree, this is decent. But PVE...

 -----------------------
 **Please share your thoughts!**

author: Theremmy
subject: Starshards build?
content_md:
While the new racial spell for NE Priests caused a lot of questions, I feel like these changes might be a great opportunity to adapt a spell that was always seems close enough to be valid, but just far enough to matter. With possibly the best looking animation of the whole of Classic, and a lore that dates back to the introduction of Night Elves in Warcraft 3!

The good news in the new changes is a lot of the new Discipline tree talents should work with Starshards, adding various buffs that potentially could trigger on ticks of channeled spell. But others might not since for some odd reason, Starshards uses Arcane damage. One of the changes to it that might not be too major would be to change that to Holy, which would still make some sense Lore wise, but definitely so mechanics wise. This could potentially give NE Priest a lovely rotation of Holy Fire, channel Starshards until Smite proc, Smite, and repeat.

I feel like the changes are so close to making this a viable really fun spec, something that should've been, imo. But again might be just one change away from being a thing. What does everyone think? I think I remember Holy Fire going through a similar change as well, with it originally being Fire damage and becoming Holy. To think that a Starshards Priest might have to use Shadow for SW:P, Fire for Holy Fire, Holy for Smite and Arcane for Starshards is a bit ridiculous.

But that still leaves me scratching my head as to how the second racial comes into play.

Anything related to the moon and stars deals arcane damage in Warcraft: see Starfire and Moonfire, the druid spells, so changing Starshards to Holy damage would break that consistency. Furthermore, Starshards is very useful in PvP as a kick bait: if a rogue kicks your starshards you're free to cast shadow and holy spells without worrying about Kick anymore for 10 seconds ; this, too, would change if Starshards is changed to a holy spell.
I get that this is useful for PvP, but otherwise why does the consistency matter? If undead priests can get a useful Shadow damage spell then why can't nelf priests get a useful Discipline damage spell? Reworking one of the nelf priest racials to be useful in the new Disc dps rotation seems perfectly fair to me

author: Amyloriley
subject: Re: Starshards build?
content_md:
I haven't had the time to play for a while, but I've been leveling an Arcane Priest for a while now.

My outdoors rotation is:

Against lower-leveled enemies:
 1. Power Word: Shield on self
 2. Holy Fire
 3. Starshards
 4. Wand

Against higher-leveled enemies:
 1. Power Word: Shield on self
 2. Holy Fire
 3. Starshards
 4. Holy Fire
 5. Starshards
 6. Wand

I think you get the gist.

When dps must increase: Add in Shadow Word: Pain
When the target must die now, because they run away to get backup: Mind Blast, now!

The disadvantage compared to Shadow Priest is, dps is roughly half of a Shadow Priest.
The advantage is, this build has almost no downtime between enemies. No need to rest and drink, just go from enemy to enemy.

Between a Starshards cast and a Holy Fire cast is about 9.5 seconds. Starshards consumes the mana at the start of the cast, Holy Fire at the end of the cast.

This gives one full tick of MP5, or two if you're willing to wait/wand another 0.5 seconds. And this is what makes this build so downtime-less.

The only spells that increase your downtime are Shadow Word: Pain and Mind Blast. So as long as you're patient, you will be rewarded out of combat.

Invest in Spirit on your gear, since it increases your MP5.

MVP talent: Spirit Tap, from the Shadow tree. That's the only Shadow talent I have. Otherwise, it's all Discipline and Holy. Almost no other talents synergize, which allows me to take standard healer build talents after Spirit Tap. Because of this, I run about 5 talent points behind the build of a standard healer. You can try other things.

This build works with only 5 talent points, so you're free to take talents however you wish with your 45 remaining ones.

One note is to end combat with Wand or Starshards, not Holy Fire. Like in, the last 10% of the enemy should not be targeted with Holy Fire. Using Starshards or Wand means the moment combat ends and Spirit Tap triggers, you're already halfway there going for your first MP5 tick.

At level 50+, this build is so efficient you're likely to have full mana when your Spirit Tap is only halfway done. Go to the next enemy, and enjoy the damage bonus from Spirit Tap. If you activate Sharshards while Spirit Tap is active, the damage bonus applies to the entire 6 second duration of your Starshards, even if Spirit Tap ends 1 second later.

 -----

My dungeon rotation is:

 - Be a standard healer with healer spells
 - Wand if nobody is dying
 - Use Starshards for that extra bit of damage when your mana is maxed out and nobody is dying

 ------

Reading the patch notes, I should rethink my build. I haven't done that part yet.

author: Amyloriley
subject: Re: Starshards build?
content_md:
Edit: just logged in and tried the new changes.

It's not too bad a change. Some bad some good.

Starshards is new very powerful!

My new solo rotation is something like

 1. Power Word: Shield
 2. Holy Fire
 3. Starshards
 4. Wand

Or against Bear-type enemies with a bigger health pool:
 1. Power Word: Shield
 2. Holy Fire
 3. Starshards
 4. Holy Fire
 5. Wand

I'm toying with the idea of adding Pain Spike or Shadow Word: Pain after Starshards, because of it being Instant speed, so it consumes mana directly after Starshard instead of waiting for a cast time to happen. MP5 that starts a few seconds earlier. :)

The new rotation *does* have some newly introduced downtime. But that's not because of mana issues, far from it. But because Starshards has a 30 second cooldown and enemies die too fast. I must wait for 5-or-so seconds before attacking another one, should I want to re-use Starshards again on time.

Ideally, it has a 25 second cooldown. It's not too bad, though it does mean I miss the Spirit Tap double damage trigger almost all the time. Except maybe when the previous enemy was a bear.

That said, I can live with the 30 second cooldown and might introduce some less mana-efficient spells in my rotation so I'm not fully mana'ed at the time I must wait these 5 seconds between combats. Hence, Pain Spike/Shadow Word: Pain.

Though of course that means enemies die even quicker, which means more waiting between combats.

Hmm... tough choice. :)

All I can think of; it's nice to be in a position where you are having downtime not because of mana problems like the other classes, but simply because of a single cooldown that might've been a few seconds too many.

author: Amyloriley
subject: Re: Starshards build?
content_md:
The sun is shining today after being cloudy all week, so I thought I make some calculations for outdoor use.

I made a little Excel to get some calculations going before I change my talents in the game.

The major advantage of current Starshards is, its 6-second channel time. It guarantees mana regen after 5 seconds equal to (1/4 of your Spirit). And if you keep wanding/shooting for four more seconds instead of casting spells, you get an extra tick of that delicious mana. Which means less downtime;
to a minimum of 24 seconds: the cooldown of Starshards minus its Channel time.
to a minimum of 20 seconds: the cooldown of Starshards minus its Channel time and 4 seconds of wanding/shooting.

From my theorycraft, I come to the following options at level 58 (my current level) and a nice round 400 Spirit (100 mana regen after Starshards).

 **My Target:** Kill a Winterspring Bear (3680 hp)

 **Starshards Shadow Build**

 1. Mind Blast
 2. Shadow Word: Pain (24 sec)
 3. Starshards

 4004.25 damage over 9 seconds spellcasting + remaining DoT
 1420 mana used

 **Starshards Improved Shadowform Build**
 *(At level 60, with 15% mana reduction.)*

 1. Mind Blast
 2. Shadow Word: Pain (24 sec)
 3. Starshards

 4004.25 damage over 9 seconds spellcasting + remaining DoT
 1297 mana used

 **Starshards Disc Build**

 1. Holy Fire
 2. Shadow Word: Pain (24 sec)
 3. Starshards

 3776.325 damage over 10.5 seconds spellcasting + remaining DoT
 1300 mana used

 4. Holy Fire (resets mp5)

 4324.95 damage over 13.5 seconds spellcasting + remaining DoT
 1530 mana used

Disc has a hybrid flavor win as you can have a Holy DoT, a Shadow DoT, and an Arcane DoT running all at the same time. But the values are otherwise all kinda similar.

Next, I'm not a guide writer. I just post my own findings. They can be wrong, take it with a grain of salt.

This build has lots of spare talents. Use them as you see fit.

 **Shadow Build Talents**

 **Shadow**

 - Tier 1: **Improved Spirit Tap** (5/5) to reduce downtime, regaining more mana out of combat
 - Tier 2: **Improved Shadow Word: Pain** (2/2) increases damage dealt per mana spent by a lot, best talent for leveling I'd say
 - Tier 3: **Improved Mind Blast** (1/5) if you want to cast another Mind Blast after using Starshards.
 - Tier 3: **Mind Flay** (0/1) I didn't take this as it's not in my build. You can take it for enemies resisting your Starshards and you want some backup to fill in the damage lost.
 - Tier 4: **Shadow Weaving** I don't think it does much. I haven't made my calculations with the talent in mind. Though at most, it increases your Shadow DoT by 6% as you might not be casting any other spells after it. Unless you Mind Blast after Starshards, at the cost of further mana regen. Your call really.
 - Tier 5: **Vampiric Embrace** (1/1) as a tax to reach Shadowform. I don't use it outdoors, as I can't move to increase the distance between enemies and me with its 1.5 sec casting time, it costs a bit mana, it triggers threat, and with the Vampiric Touch talent the return is like 20 mana saved after the bear is dead.
 - Tier 6: **Darkness** (5/5) +10% damage to Mind Blast and Shadow Word: Pain.
 - Tier 7: **Shadowform** (1/1) +15% damage to Mind Blast and Shadow Word: Pain. At level 60, 15% mana reduction.

 **Discipline Talents**

 - Tier 1: **Wand Specialization** and **Piercing Light**. Piercing Light I believe also reduces Starshards' resist, since it's a Discipline spell. Wand Spec, well, wand. **Mental Agility** only affects Power Word: Shield, not Starshards.
 - Tier 2: No talents are required.
 - Tier 3: **Meditation** and **Inner Focus** can be fun.
 - Tier 4: Regarding **Purifying Flames**. The maximized use of the 12% bonus to Holy spells in my calculations (Holy Fire, Smite, Smite, Smite, Smite, Holy Fire) cost exactly the same amount of mana as (Holy Fire, Shadow Word: Pain, Starshards) for roughly 750 less damage. Swap out a Smite of Mind Blast if you wish, but now the 12% bonus has even less of a total effect. Either way, with Starshards you save 2 talent points that you can put somewhere else.

 **Most mana-efficient spells at level 58**
 *(written as damage per mana. 2.00 equals 2 damage dealt for every 1 mana spent.)*

 - Shadow Word: Pain (+talent: 24 seconds) (3.02)
 - Starshards (2.77)
 - Mind Flay (+Darkness, +Shadow Form) (2.50)
 - Shadow Word: Pain (not talented, 18 seconds) (2.27)
 - Mind Blast (+Darkness, +Shadow Form) (1.85)

 **Disc/Holy Build Talents**

TODO

But... without Purifying Flames to get excited about, the deeper Disc tree has little to offer. **Force of Will** adds +5% damage, competing with the +25% from Darkness + Shadow Form.

Force of Will-talented Holy Fire competes with an non-Darkness non-Shadow Form Mind Blast in damage, for less mana but with a longer casting time. Between those, I'd choose Holy Fire every time. But looking at a fully-buffed Mind Blast, the competition looks interesting at least, in my opinion.

 **Starshards** (+Force of Will) 2.97)
 **Shadow Word: Pain** (+Force of Will, 24 seconds) (2.54)
 **Holy Fire** (+Force of Will) (2.39)
 **Smite** (+Force of Will) (2.02) (note: in TurtleWoW, Smite stats are buffed compared to vanilla!)
 **Shadow Word: Pain** (+Force of WIll, 18 seconds) (1.90)
 **Mind Blast** (+Force of Will) (1.55) (note how in the Shadow tree, Mind Blast deals more damage for the same amount of mana)

In the Holy Tree, important talents are:

 - Tier 2: **Divine Fury** (5/5), decreases the casting time of Holy Fire.
 - Tier 4: **Spiritual Guidance** (5/5), with 400 Spirit you should have +100 damage per spell. I have not made my calculations above with this in mind because it's so different for everybody else.
 - Tier 5: **Spirit of Redemption** (1/1), for a +5% Spirit increase.

With this build, you have free talents to spend for a more healer-focused build. In Vanilla, in dungeons you'd be a healer sacrificing 10% of all heal potential for a Starshards cast when your mana is high and everyone's health is high. Help out the damage dealers a bit. The healing loss would come from Spiritual Healing, taking Spirit Tap instead.

In TurtleWoW, the gap is a bit larger. No Spiritual Healing means a 30% loss of healing potential. And the capstone not being Lightwell but Proclaim Champion might also make you less of a healer. I don't know how well you can still heal in TurtleWoW with this Starshards build, but at least you've got *some* healing talents.

Yeah, I still don't know which way to go. Shadow or Disc/Holy. Shadow deals more damage as is without high Spirit gear, but you can't access both Spiritual Guidance and Inner Focus/Meditation at the same time.

I haven't looked at Spiritual Guidance+Shadow Form instead of Meditation. Still work to do figuring it all out.

With this build, you have free talents to spend for a more healer-focused build. In Vanilla, in dungeons you'd be a healer sacrificing 10% of all heal potential for a Starshards cast when your mana is high and everyone's health is high. Help out the damage dealers a bit. The healing loss would come from Spiritual Healing, taking Spirit Tap instead.

In TurtleWoW, the gap is a bit larger. No Spiritual Healing means a 30% loss of healing potential. And the capstone not being Lightwell but Proclaim Champion might also make you less of a healer. I don't know how well you can still heal in TurtleWoW with this Starshards build, but at least you've got some healing talents.

Yeah, I still don't know which way to go. Shadow or Disc/Holy. Shadow deals more damage as is without high Spirit gear, but you can't access both Spiritual Guidance and Inner Focus/Meditation at the same time.

I haven't looked at Spiritual Guidance+Shadow Form instead of Meditation. Still work to do figuring it all out.

author: Silverleafeon
subject: Priest quest idea for different racial spell
content_md:
What if priests had the option to replace/learn a racial spell from a different race? Like a Night Elf learning Desperate Prayer, a Human learning Devouring Plague, etc.

I know the idea is each race is supposed to be unique, but I've always found this particular aspect to be a bit too restrictive. Arguably, it would be more realistic and lore friendly to be able to learn the teachings of other priests from different races. As a priest, adventuring out in the world, it makes sense that you'd come across different ideas and beliefs, and perhaps you would like to learn more about them.

I think a class quest should become available to priests at level 30 that allows the player to seek out a trainer of another race who sends you off on a quest chain to learn a new racial spell. For opposite faction spells, there might be a neutral npc that gives you the quest.

author: Bigsmerf
subject: Re: Why Nerf Shadow with Martyrdom?
content_md:
Weakening strong specs is a good idea. I support this.

The issue arises when you buff weaker specs (or even already strong specs) to levels that make the previously mentioned nerf unnecessary and harmful to balance. CC2 did this to some extent with ele sham. Their burst was nerfed hard, and their niche of being a glass cannon has been replaced by specs like smite priest or boomkin or mages who alternatively have great defensive/escape tools. I'm sure there's other examples but I'm just scratching the surface with a basic idea of what the PvP situation seems to be.

author: Caracole
subject: Re: Priest t2.5 need adjustments
content_md:
T2.5 is AQ40 level, I don't see why it should be necessarily better than Naxx gear. Otherwise, we can just call it a day at C'thun (who, anyway, has most of the bis caster gear). The T2.5 leggings are good, and it's good that leggings of polarity are better.. although that's debatable given how searing light (and crit) was nerfed.

The 'enemy Chastise' (pvp) was problematic because cumulating 3s + 2s (on T2.5 bonus) gave an instant 30 yards 5s-long disorient to the disci priest, and that was overkill. I get it. I would argue the problem was not the baseline 3s (which, reminder, costs 1.5s of gcd) but the T2.5 bonus. I don't think the baseline needed to be nerfed.

Anyway, what's really problematic is that our capstone spell, the 'friendly Chastise' (pve), is so weak, it's virtually useless, besides eventually helping tank generate aggro on pull. Chastise is not a buff but a dps transfer with a loss for the raid damage. 6s are too short to justify spending a gcd on it. 8s are still too short to justify getting the T2.5 bonus for it. It needs a huge boost (including via the T2.5 bonus) if we want to make disci priest an actual support dps, possibly synergizing it with Enlighten to give the disci dps an edge over the disci/holy hybrid priest (healer) who can also Enlighten.

Also, if the disci gets 'off tier sets', why doesn't it have a T3.5 set? Everybody else does.

> Reverting chantise to 3s baseline and adjusting t2.5 bonus seems reasonable to me. Maybe further incentivise shielding? Would make sense in PVE as well.

Shielding is for emergencies and we don't need PvP buffs. We shouldn't be investing in it when:
1. Our capstone [Chastise] is next to useless in PvE.
2. On a single target: We are ranked 19 out of all 22 dps specs (c.f. last week Patchwerk logs), we are only above Moonkins, Survival hunters and Subtlety rogues.
3. Our support ability is not unique, [Enlighten] can easily be provided by healer priests and the aforementioned rank19 comes from self-enlightened smite priests (i.e. providing NO raid support, basically a mage but with 3/4 of the dps).
4. On AoEs: We lost what made [Holy Nova] unique pre-cc2, which is that it didn't generate threat.
5. The original cc2 crit-spec design was abandoned, even though we had very average endgame raid dps. It was just pvp boys complaining they got double critted in BGs.
6. We have no useful T2.5 bonus, also due to point 1.
7. Most of the priest dps T3 and T3.5 are forbidden to us as they only provide shadow spell power.
8. Our only tier set (T2.5) has NO healing power. Other hybrid rdps (Moonkins and Elemental shamans) have healing power on their tier sets AND they have T3 and T3.5 sets. What's up with that?
The smite priest is a wreck.

author: Caracole
subject: Re: Priest t2.5 need adjustments
content_md:
> **amanagor wrote: Wed Dec 04, 2024 2:11 pm**
> its not about getting double critted in pvp. it was beyong absurd. priest would insta cc you from range, cast holy fire into an instant smite, and regardless of if the smite crit or not, you were dead. without being able to do anything about it as all that damage lands at the same time while you're cc

Well, if it wasn't about double critting, we can just remove the internal cd on searing light... unless the problem is having instant smites altogether, in which case, let's remove it and be done with it.

The problem was the 30yards 5seconds cc (with T2.5 bonus), not the damage where we are behind, compared to other rdps. I'm not asking for "more damage" for the sake of it, but rather for gameplay changes: committing to the original crit-based build (while keeping the pre-cc2 smite base damage), better scaling (so we remain competitive endgame, almost all our talents offer 'flat bonuses', with the exception of searing light which was nerfed), better options for itemization (tier sets, actual bonuses and better valuing crit) and a capstone that offers actual support to the raid.

I wouldn't mind lowering smite base damage below vanilla levels to compensate for it, if that means having a more dynamic gameplay where crit enhances not just damage (other crit-specs get 200%+ damage on crit, we're fine with 150%) but also mobility (via instant casts) and mana management (SL causes us to cast 2/1.5=33% more smites, saving 20% mana per smite is not really a bonus).

author: Quidoba
subject: Re: Priest t2.5 need adjustments
content_md:
I don't get how a chastise into a DPS dump combo, is any different than a wyvern sting into an aimed shot/multi/auto attack combo from a hunter, or warlock death coil into dots+fear, or a mage sheep into slows and instant cast spells.   All of these ranged are doing way better damage in Naxx, and will scale better into kara40 gear.

Balancing a fully progressed classic server for PVP is impossible.  Especially considering we don't have PVP gear with stats like resilience to combat the raid gear arms race.  We should NEVER break PVE balance for the sake of PVP.  If you can keep PVE balanced, and still balance PVP oriented abilities then do that.

The Searing light nerf was fully unjustified, and probably the worst decision that could have been made by the team, given the context of gear scaling already being a problem for smite.

If Smite priests were doing too much DPS in PVE, then any nerfs should have been targeted at flat bonus damage that is NOT part of the scaling potential.  Smite priests come into 60 with too much damage, but flatten out really fast.

If Chastise needs to be taken out of a smite priests PVP toolkit do that.

Smite priest needs either more useful PVE utility (to justify the low top-end DPS), or to have it's scaling potential improved.

I agree smite is a wreck.
 1. lacks identity
 2. poor gear scaling
 3. poorly itemized gear options
 4. lacks raid damage or compelling utility to justify raid spot

author: Caracole
subject: Re: shadow gear progression
content_md:
Gear and talent changes didn't changing anything regarding how to gear a shadow priest, even relatively to Vanilla WoW.
You just get 5% hit, stack spell power and more or less ignore everything else.

I know of this spreadsheet [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ ... id=0#gid=0](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1F1IVqSt1MEJ9yjZ9rn1aKGIWNkJiA_CNmn6fLUpakb4/edit?gid=0#gid=0)
It's quite old but nothing substantial has changed since then. Given the buff of mind flay scaling, crit is probably even less important than before (compared to spell power). Note that the spreadsheet does not attribute any importance to hit%, it's only comparing the rest. Hit is obviously very important, but reaching the cap should be easy on TWoW.
Don't take it as gospel either, totally ignoring intell and mp5 (e.g. flarecore set) can lead to mana problems on long fights. But it's a good start.

author: Matches
subject: Spirit of Redemption - be better with 5% spirit only
content_md:
As a healer Priest, I stack spirit for mana regen.

Talent Spirit of Redemption is for me a pain in the neck - I play AV mainly, and that for PvE, and when I'm dead, I want to come back to life ASAP, not after 10 seconds.

In any event I find the talent pretty much a non-starter because most of your time is spend trying to find someone to heal and then your time is up.

However, the talent now gives 5% spirit so I've kinda gotta take it, which kinda sucks.  I'd be *much* happier if you gave me the 5% spirit and did *NOT* give me the 10 seconds being useless.

As an aside, I note I had 401 spirit, and adding the talent took me to 417 spirit, which is not 5%.

(Divine Spirit is worth 40 spirit, in and of itself, and I now as expected get 42 spirit from it, so that looks to be working correctly.)

author: Mosttrustworthy
subject: Re: Chastise Self macro
content_md:
No add-ons required, although I do like SuperMacro.

/script if UnitIsEnemy("target") then TargetUnit("player") CastSpellByName("Chastise") TargetLastEnemy() else CastSpellByName("Chastise") end

If your target is an enemy, it targets yourself and casts Chastise, then re-targets the enemy.
Otherwise is just casts Chastise.
It even fits into the default character limit, at 141 characters. There's even room to add DoEmote("Roar") somewhere.

author: Hawkbutt
subject: Re: Talent Tree Healer Priest
content_md:
Mostly it doesn't matter. You can be fully specced into the Shadow tree and still heal fine in dungeons.

Early talents to help with leveling is Spirit Tap 5/5 and Wand Specialization 2/2.
Disc/Holy trees both offer healing benefits.

Disc:
Mental Agility - reduced mana cost
Improved Power Word: Fortitude - bigger buffs
Meditation - mana regen
Improved Inner Fire - bigger self buff
Inner Focus - mana free spell
Enlighten, Mental Strength, Chastise - all good talents with utility

Holy:
Improved Renew - more healing
Holy Focus - avoid interruption (good for solo too, I pick this over Divinity as you won't be stacking crit while leveling)
Divine Fury - faster heals
Improved Healing - reduced mana cost
Spiritual Healing - bigger heals
Proclaim Champion - may be useful on a squishy tank but it tries to do everything where it may have been more useful to do 1 thing really well (the fact they are nerfing enlighten to try and get people to spec into Proclaim Champion should tell you everything you need to know)

I leveled a healer priest before cc2 so be a bit skeptycal with what I say.
In dungeons, renew was a huge help for me but for unique reasons:
You can renew and heal a tank in case of extreme pressure but in a dungeon this barely happens.
What I used DOWNRANKED renew for:
 * Putting it on DPS above half health so they heal up by the end of the fight.
 * Some heals while moving, making sure everyone enters the next pull with full hp. Specially relevant for faster runs.
 * A toy for warlocks. You see a lock in your party life tap -> Downranked renew immediately.

Raids used to be different. There was always a full T2 priest who spammed renew with the set bonus. No idea how it works now.

tldr: Renew is really useful for dungeons, mostly downranked. Non-targeted DPS, moving and healing, warlocks.

+1: As others said, you can pre-hot a tank before pull. But have a threatmeter then, it can generate a surprising amount of threat.

Many dungeons you can even heal mostly using renew. Big renew to tank, some smaller to DPS if needed and wand. With a bit of experience you can abuse 5 sec spirit regen this way and never go oom.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Please make Vampire Touch  as a Instant cast again
content_md:
Painspike can be coppled with mindblast for relatively big burst. Shadowpriest never was a burst class before painspike, but unfortunately thanks to the huge + shadow amplification shadows had and access to inner focus, they could have a lesser version of the feared elemental shaman nuke combo if they were afforded a brief timewindow to cast. Which wasnt all that rare considering power word shield, psychic scream and blackout could open up windows for it.

So we had a class that is designed to win by outlasting and that has 2-3k burstdmg (MB +Spike) at the ready (depending if you crit or not).
I have the feeling painspike was designed to help shadowpriest in pve fish for killing blows in order to use spirit tap, but it seems to be largely inconsequential in that role. Mana isnt an issue anymore anyway.

Further daming the spell is the fact that while it sounds like it doesnt generate progress unless you kill the target before the 5 seconds of healing window expires, this is wrong. The healing is equal to the base damage the spell deals. Thanks to crits, shadowform and other shadow amplifications you will always deal more damage than the target heals. (Or at least that used to be the case, havent played priest in half a year)

Considering painspike was added shadowpriest didnt need to outlast 100% of an enemies hp, but rather outlast ~80% and then finish you off with an instant. Thats akin to a 20% dmg amplification for pvp purposes.

I would have prefered seeing PS go than doctoring with VE, but under the constraints that PS stays, i think VE nerf was not the dumbest move for pvp balance. What however was is not applying the same caution that was made with Shadowpriest & Ememental for PvP in 1.17.2 to literally any Spec. Creating extremely bursty encounters all over the place

UPDATES | Dated: April 1th 2025
PRIEST

These changes primarily aim to improve Discipline Priest's personal damage and support capabilities and to improve Shadow Priest's Player versus Player environment power as the changes brought with the initial class changes release ended up being harsher than we've intended it to be.

Pain Spike: Spellpower scaling increased from 25% to 43%.

Developer Comment: The earlier scaling reduction on Pain Spike ended up being more harsh than we've intended with it compounding with the cooldown increase, so we're increasing its spellpower scaling back up.

 -----------------
They made it very clear that they would rather turn Pain Spike into a nuclear bomb than give your good old Vampire Touch back.

author: Elesion
subject: Re: Flash heal on the new set => holy priest is now braindead
content_md:
> **Terrydavis wrote: Tue Apr 01, 2025 5:26 pm**
> im so tired dude and now you give us THE MOST NOOB SKILL OF ALL: FLASH HEAL on the new set?
>  i had to read the set bonus 3 times dude you can not be serious... i dont know what to say ...
>  you remove all skill from the class. just get a healbot and spam flash heal, thats all.
>  its not that flash heal suddenly becomes amazing, rather my problem is youre promoting the complete noob play style of priest. youre supposed to make fun of flash heal spammers, not spam flash heal. now youre supporting this garbage play style, i just cant.

This is written harshly, but also truthfully. CC2 has dumbed down healing a lot. Due to the general dps increase fights are now so short that mana economy (previously the core gameplay mechanic of healers) barely matters anymore.
You cannot balance healers like damage dealers. More damage onto the boss is always better. But damage-taken is a limited quantity. So the goal of healer gameplay is not to maximize your personal output, but to find and coordinate synergies with other healers to make best use of their respective strengths and weaknesses.
And that means traditionally healers would prioritize efficiency over through-put. That's the whole idea behind downranking and why every healer learns to intuitively do it.

Spamming Flash Heal is indeed something that should be looked down upon because it disregards mana efficiency in favor of through-put. It ignores the vast majority of your class' toolkit. It maximizes personal healing on the meters but usually that means you just push other healers into doing more overhealing, so the raid doesn't actually benefit. You spend more resources to do the same.
So Flash Heal is very deliberately expensive. You pay more for speed in case of emergencies. If there is no immediate emergency, you should use a slower more efficient heal. And that not only rewards you with a better mana economy, lower consumable usage, and better cooperation with other healers, it also rewards skillful predictive healing. Anyone can mash a one-button healbot and watch it snipe people to full, but at that point why even show up to play?

The same issue happened with Druids. Developers saw that Regrowth was rarely used due to its high mana cost. So they lowered the mana cost by about 30% across the board. But Regrowth has always been an awesome and very strong heal spell with a short cast time that was expensive as a trade-off. Now they removed that trade-off and suddenly a whole new generation of Druids plays the class like Paladin - just spam a 1.5s heal spell to top off people. That change killed Healing Touch as a major style of druid healing. Why be slow and mana efficient when you can be fast and not run out of mana either? The first rewards skill, the second is brain dead and tops meters. Easy choice what people are doing now. But over-all a very bad development for the class.

tl;dr: Every healing class has its strengths and weaknesses, and a diverse toolkit available. The fun and skillful way of healing is using all that potential to its fullest. And that usually means very fast spells should be prohibitively expensive as a trade-off. Don't treat healing like damage dealing and make everyone maximize output in the dumbest most brain-dead and most easily-automated way.

author: Forumdweller
subject: Disc priests are insane in pvp and are stronger than shadow
content_md:
Every priest is playing disc spec in pvp over shadow because the damage and survivability and team utility is unparalleled. You can literally spam rank 1 flash of light to get the proc before even engaging in the fight and then
cast holy fire into insta cast smite into another insta cast smite if you crit which is enough to kill anyone.

It's absurd when you compare it to nightfall which has a 4% chance to proc every 3 second tick on a dispellable dot..

I recommend changing the searing light talent from proccing on holy/disc crits to instead functioning more like warlocks nightfall. This will keep the theme you guys are very clearly aiming for with priest being an offensive healer without making them a literal immortal dps class in pvp. And adding some form of counter in the form of dispelling the priests renews.

So in raids or BG's you just renew everyone and then every time renew ticks you have a small chance to get a searing light insta proc. More heals = more procs.

author: Tess322
subject: Discipline Priest KZ40 Edition
content_md:
I would like to raise some findings and glaring issues I found by progressing KZ40 as a Discipline priest (Smite) and provide possible solutions.
Discipline is not a popular spec in PVE and for a good reason. I believe it can be remedied with the right changes.

KZ40 overview
Discipline is an extremely underplayed spec in higher tiers and for good reasons. Currently one of the main issues is mana and this is even more evident during progress. For Disc to be a viable pick in your raid roster you need to use Major Mana Pots, Teas in combination with items such as Robe of Sacrifice or Darkmoon Card: Blue Dragon. Without these additional items the priest will run out of mana just by doing its normal rotation.
This brings me to another issue, utility. As its stands Discipline brings the following utility: Enlightenment, Chastise, Shielding, Dispelling and Off healing. At the moment due to mana issues Shielding and Off healing is out of the picture as if this situation occurs where these are needed priest will run out of mana and be useless for the rest of the fight. Dispelling is not as much an issue but still affects and is affected by your mana.
Compared to Shadow which brings: Vampiric Embrace, Shadow Weaving, Shielding, Dispelling and Offhealing, you can see why it is an obvious choice over Discipline.

Another issue is that at the moment Discipline deals less damage than Shadow (with full debuffs on target) whilst not bringing the passive healing and mana regen. Discipline needs to sacrifice DPS in order to heal or shield their targets. This issue will only fester as more raid tiers are added as the problem is more a scaling issue than a flat damage one.

Suggested changes
 **Searing Light**
Mana cost discount increased from 20% to 50%
 *This would greatly help with the mana situation as this talent was very overnerfed. I would not be afraid to put it to as much as 70% but that would require testing on lower gear tiers.*

 **Resurgent Shield**
Change the 10% bonus damage and healing from damage absorbed by Shield to flat 10% spell damage and healing bonus.
 *Currently Resurgent Shield is never picked as the bonus provides around 140 spell power with uptime of 8 seconds requiring 1.5s GCD as well making it not a competitive choice versus Spiritual Guidance which provides around 80 spell power on average with 100% uptime.*

Change the 25% mana cost refund to - When your Power Word: Shield is broken, your (holy) damaging spells restore 15% of its base mana cost.
 *This would ensure the usage of shields by Discipline priests as it would help with the massive 450 mana cost in an interactive way. Yes it would make the talent unusable by healers - another way preserving the talent for healers is to make healing spells to proc this effect as well but with a lower chance.*

 **Missing Tier Set**
Gearing is another issue Discipline has in endgame, the last tier was T2.5 which is not competitive in KZ40 due to lack of worthwhile effects and stats.
As with other specs such as Feral (Cat), Discipline can folllow the same pattern - meaning having tier sets in X.5 tiers -> implementing T3.5 for Discipline priest.
 *Note: Set should have general spell power instead of holy spell power as Discipline uses Shadow Word: Pain frequently.*

author: Vainamoinen77
subject: A small suggestion concerning Night Elves and their bows
content_md:
Priest is an unique class by virtue of having access to two extra racial spells meant to represent their race's religious culture, and Night Elf priests might be the most peculiar of them all: they can use bows!

 **THE ISSUE**
While I do greatly appreciate the nod towards Tyrande and WCIII in general, I feel that the implementation leaves much to be desired. Simply put, there aren't many reasons to make use of that special proficiency. Being able to cast Searing Shot while on the move is cute, but not at all worth the opportunity cost of missing out on a wand's useful stats while also having to deal with a bow's minimum range, ammo requirments and much lower dps. Perhaps the spell could be made more worthwile by tweaking the numbers, but honestly overcharging it seems like a clunky solution. I'm aware that this ability is mostly here for roleplay purposes, but given that the other racial spell available to Night Elves is also highly situational and rarely used, they could use a little push, if only to make bow-wielding priestess of Elune a more common sight.

 **A POSSIBLE SOLUTION**
My humble suggestion would be to reduce the opportunity cost rather than increasing the pay-off, or in other words, to implement a small selection of bows that a priest might want to use. Instead of making Searing Shot stronger, which might lead a Night Elf priest to begrudgingly wield a bow to gain access to it, make them want the bow and let Searing Shot be a novel, situational spell they get to enjoy along with it. I'm aware that this is trickier than it sounds: those bows can't be added to dungeon or raid loot, as they would be worthless to the overwhelming majority of the playerbase, and they can't be too good either; having devouring plague being a racial spell is polarizing enough as it is, no need to make the pendulum swing in the opposite direction. Luckily, I think that there is an easy way to ensure that Night Elves priests get to actually enjoy their added proficiency without disrupting the game's balance or the loot tables.

 **IMPLEMENTATION**
For leveling priests, a few blue bows with a level-appropriate quantity of int/spirit, maybe some spell damage and healing after level 40, could be sold by the darnassus quartermaster. At higher levels, the same quartermaster could offer two or three little quests that would require the player to turn in a wand that they would want to get anyway (for example, Touch of Chaos) and gain a roughly equivalent bow in exchange. This would also leave some room for experimentation if so desired; you could have for example a bow with an on use effect that changes the damage type of your next starshards, or one that does not consume arrows. They really do not need to be especially good, but simply being able to wield a bow without making your character weaker in the process would go a long way to make that special ability feel useful.

Anyway, just my two cents.

author: Thaladar
subject: Re: A small suggestion concerning Night Elves and their bows
content_md:
As a fellow Night Elf priest, I actually love Searing Shot and the bow mechanic:

•	No GCD lockout: Shooting bows doesn’t trigger the global cooldown, so I can shoot and immediately cast spells – very smooth in both PvP and PvE.

•	Instant Smite synergy: One of my favorite tricks is shooting sitting players because any hit on a sitting target is a guaranteed crit → which can proc an Instant Smite. It’s such a satisfying combo and feels like a unique “priest thing.”

•	Great vs clothies: Even without attack power gear, I’ve crit up to ~600 with Searing Shot, which hits surprisingly hard on low armor targets.

I agree it could scale better (maybe use spell damage instead of AP and convert the damage type to Holy), but in PvP it already adds fun utility and flavor. I run stamina-heavy bows and use Searing Shot on cooldown.

Even in PvE it’s nice for mana regen with improved wand/bow talents + paladin Seal of Wisdom, letting me regen mana and swap back to healing instantly since there’s no wand GCD lockout.

author: Zitronenhaze
subject: Mind Blast Threat Multiplier - Threat in PvE in general
content_md:
Hello!

Can we talk about shadow priest threat generation in PvE?

 ----------
Threat Calculation:

Mind Blast has a 200% Threat Multiplier.

Vampiric Embrace heals for 25% of the dmg dealt.
Improved VE heals for 30% of the dmg dealt per person in grp.
So if your group drops in hp, its 150% of the dmg dealt in heal threat.

Then in addition to that you generate threat for the mana restored, which is another 2% per player in grp.
So in total its 10% of the dmg dealt.

So in Total Threat:

 100% of the dmg dealt + 150% of the dmg dealt in healing + 10% of dmg in mana reg = 260% per dmg
In additon you deal 200% more dmg threat every 6 seconds with Mind Blast.
Which results in more than 300% threat.

 -----------
Reasoning:

I dont see a reason for shadow priests to do so much threat, while only being middle of the pack in dmg.
Even compared to all other casters, which have lots of tools to combat threat.
Such as Set Bonuses that reduce threat, etc.

Meanwhile the Shadow Priest Set in Kara even reduces your Mind Blast Cooldown, so you generate even more with your 200% threat multiplier on it.

In Vanilla the Mind Blast Threat Multiplier wasnt that big of a problem, since it had way lower spellpower coefficent.
In Twow several spells got adjustments, but the threat multiplier didnt.

Please dont bring up Priest Tank, thats really just a fraction of all priest players.

 ---------------
Possible Solutions that are in the game now (Spoiler, they arent close to enough):

Now you could say, just take all the anti threat talents there are.
But in reality you dont want to go into the disc tree second anymore, for the extra spellpower from spirit in the holy tree.

And in the shadow tree, its so akwardly placed, that you need to take points out of Shadow Weaving, Mind Blast(your best dmg/gcd ability, which also has a 6 sec Cooldown) or Spellhit.

Other classes can help, like Paladin's Salvation that is in every raid.
Second a Shaman in the Shadow Priest group, which is much much more rare.

 -----------
Possible Solutions that could be implemented, in my opinion:

Remove the Mind Blast Threat Multiplier
Reduce the healing done by improved VE
Give improved VE anti threat build in
Reduce points needed in a shadow talent, that allows to spec into anti threat,
without losing identity giving or damage talents.

 -----------

Sorry for the wall of text, but i really think its a problem when the best thing to do is not pressing your buttons.
I hope some Twow Dev takes the time to read this and reply :)

Kind regards,
Zitronenhaze

author: Thaladar
subject: Bring Back Disc-Accessible Mana Burn Talent (or Move Shadow Version Down)
content_md:
Right now, Improved Mana Burn sits in the Shadow tree, and this has had a big impact on priest PvP builds. If you want to go Disc for support, use Chastise, and still have a viable Mana Burn, you end up sacrificing Holy Nova and other key Holy talents. That’s a big tradeoff and it’s one that basically killed Mana Burn as a practical spell since you’re stuck with the slow 3-second cast.

Suggestions:

 * Move Improved Mana Burn back into the Discipline tree, or
 * Keep it in the Shadow tree but shift it to the 2nd row so it’s more accessible to support builds.

This would make priests better at supporting their teams and give them a needed tool to counter overtuned casters without being forced into a pure Shadow build.

I get that Mana Burn is not fun to play against, but if that’s the concern, maybe we look at other mana drain mechanics like Hunter Viper Sting, which is instant and has no real drawback. If priests need to stand still for 3 seconds to drain mana, maybe hunters should too.
